claims.claim_text: The CIR combustion chamber has a volume of 90 L.
The CIR chamber can operate at approximately 0 to 9 atm.
For FLEX, safety analysis reduced the maximum working pressure to approximately 3 atm.
FLEX tests in the TP were run at pressures between 0.70 and 3.05 atm, most between 0.7 and 1 atm.
Deployment needles are stainless-steel tubes of 250 µm outside diameter with specially treated ends.
Two hot-wire igniters are located 180° to each other in the same plane as the deployment needles.
Fiber-supported tests used an 80 µm support fiber.
The 80 µm support fiber is silicon carbide.
claims.note: Not stated in the TP; stated in a FLEX-team conference paper seen only as a search snippet.

claims.claim_text: HiBMs droplet-size uncertainty was estimated at ±50 µm; coverage factor and distribution are not stated.
HiBMs minimum spatial resolution is stated as ±29.5 µm (FOV 30.25 mm, 1024 px).
claims.note: Inconsistent with the 32.5 px/mm scale factor in §3.1.1 (see DSC-006).

claims.claim_text: LLUV flame-size uncertainty was estimated at ±200 µm; minimum spatial resolution ±113 µm (57.8 mm, 512 px).
MDCA colour-camera flame-size uncertainty was estimated at ±250 µm; minimum spatial resolution ±146 µm (93.2 mm, 640 px).
The LLUV threshold represents the outer edge of OH* chemiluminescence and likely overestimates a measure based on maximum radial intensity.
Colour-camera flame diameters are typically about three-fourths of LLUV flame diameters, with a larger discrepancy for sooting heptane flames.
The MDCA radiometers were not sensitive enough to provide reliable quantitative information; radiometer data are not reported.
The g-environment was low enough that buoyant flow could be considered negligible, but g-jitter caused droplet drift, potentially out of the camera FOV.
When a droplet drifts out of a camera's FOV the data from that view end or show a gap; this is not the end of the test.
Time zero in Appendix B plots and the D₀ of Table IX correspond to when the igniters were turned on.

sources.locator: App. A.1, p. 19; App. B, p. 29

claims.claim_text: The Table IX burning rate is an average from a linear fit of D² versus time from shortly after ignition to extinction.
Table IX ambient composition is reconstructed from detailed records of chamber fill, recirculation, filter and combustion history.
Cameras record for a preset time, typically on the order of 40 s.
Data recording starts before droplet deployment; ignition follows deployment; igniters are then turned off and retracted.
A conformal coating on the fuel needles dissolved/flaked into the fuel in the tests reported; deployed droplets contained an unknown amount of it.
Per the TP authors, burning-rate constants and flame sizes were minimally influenced by the needle contaminant.
claims.note: Authors' assertion based on testing and analysis.

claims.claim_text: Per the TP authors, disruptive extinction of methanol is probably due to the needle contaminant; for heptane no conclusion can be drawn.
Tests FLEX–001 to –009 used a 1/30 s shutter with image distortion from igniters and flame radiation; later tests used 1/1000 s, giving more accurate droplet size data.
After visible flame extinction in some large heptane tests, continued vaporization and vapour-cloud formation were observed, which the authors describe as indicative of cool flame burning.

sources.locator: Fig. 39 caption p. 63; Fig. 66 p. 90; Fig. 201 p. 225

claims.note: An inference by the authors, not a direct measurement of a cool flame.

GRI-Mech 3.0 is a methane/natural-gas mechanism and is not an appropriate default for methanol or n-heptane FLEX simulations.

claims.claim_text: Natural convection destroys the spherical symmetry of droplet combustion in normal gravity; microgravity experiments afford spherical symmetry.
claims.note: Added in M5 (used by the burn timeline).

claims.claim_text: After deployment the droplet is misshaped by the needle retraction but assumes the expected spherical shape within approximately 1 s.
claims.note: Added in M5 (used by the burn timeline).

claims.claim_text: For heptane tests with significant soot luminosity (not visible in the LLUV, dominant in the colour camera), the peak of the soot luminosity is typically inside the blue flame envelope.
claims.note: Added in M5 (used by the burn timeline).

claims.claim_text: Both flame-diameter measurements are of the outer edge of the flame; the colour-camera diameters are the smaller of the two.
claims.note: Added in M5 (used by the burn timeline).

claims.claim_text: The CIR diagnostics include a backlit view of the droplet (HiBMs, laser-diode illumination at 650–660 nm operated below lasing threshold) and an orthogonal view of the flame.
claims.note: Added in M5 (3D layout).

claims.claim_text: The MDCA colour camera has a zoom lens and a white LED on the MDCA; the LED is on during droplet formation and is turned off immediately before deployment and ignition, when the camera zooms out to a field of view of approximately 110 by 90 mm.

claims.claim_text: The TP introduces spherically symmetric droplet combustion as a classical problem first addressed by Godsave (1952), Hall and Diederichsen (1953) and Spalding (1952, 1953).
claims.note: Basis for calling the D²-law baseline 'the classical theory the TP cites'; the TP itself presents no model equations.

claims.claim_text: The FLEX tests were burned at 'ambient temperature'; the TP gives no numerical value, so the D²-law baseline assumes 298.15 K.
claims.note: The 298.15 K value is an assumption of this release, not a TP value.

claims.claim_text: Fuel boiling points, latent heats and liquid densities, and the cp, conductivity and viscosity of N2, O2, CO2 and He used by the D²-law baseline, are CoolProp 8.0.0 evaluations at 1 atm (data/model/d2law_properties.json).
claims.note: Reproducible by re-running the generator, which refuses other CoolProp versions. Fuel-vapour properties are not used: the methanol and n-heptane equations are valid only to 620 K and 600 K.

claims.claim_text: Standard enthalpy of combustion of liquid n-heptane: -4.825 to -4.809 MJ/mol (midpoint -4817 kJ/mol used).
claims.note: Tertiary source; the range is carried into the model's Q_variant low/high option.

claims.claim_text: Standard enthalpy of combustion of liquid methanol: -726.1 kJ/mol (S44, from formation enthalpies) and -727 kJ/mol (S44), but -715.0 kJ/mol in S45; -726.1 kJ/mol is used, the spread is carried as the low/high option.
claims.note: See DSC-027.

claims.claim_text: The D²-law educational baseline (openflex/d2law.py 1.0.0) passes 24 code-verification checks (conservation residuals, boundary and jump conditions, RK4 convergence order, fixed point, invariances, hand calculation). It is not validated against FLEX.

sources.locator: Table IX (printed values used only for the comparison, not to set the model)

claims.note: Record: data/verification/d2law_code_verification.json. Code verification shows the equations are solved correctly, not that they describe FLEX.

claims.claim_text: At the printed conditions of the Table IX tests, the baseline's burning-rate constant exceeds the printed K for every test with both values: model/printed median 2.1 (methanol, 151 tests) and 4.3 (n-heptane, 109 tests).
claims.note: Comparison, not validation (data/analysis/d2law_vs_table_ix.csv). Expected directions of error include gas properties of hot air rather than fuel vapour and products, and no radiative loss; these are not quantified here.
